issues.description: Attribute type inconsistency for Ride.abbreviation: The UML in problem_statement.md declares Ride.abbreviation as type 'char' (problem_statement.md lines 21-24). In the solution, src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java declares the field 'private String abbreviation' (lines 5-6) and the Ride constructor and getter use String (constructor at line 8, getter at line 17). At the same time src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java declares its constructor parameter as 'char abbreviation' (line 7) and calls super(name, abbreviation) (line 8). This mismatch between 'char' and 'String' across the UML and solution classes (and between Ride and RollerCoaster) will cause compilation errors and confuses students which type to implement for abbreviation.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the type of 'abbreviation' consistent across UML, Ride, and subclasses. Two viable actions:
1) Align with the UML (preferred if exercise intends 'char'): change Ride.abbreviation to type 'char', update Ride constructor signature to Ride(String name, char abbreviation), change getAbbreviation() to return char, and update all subclasses' constructors (e.g., RollerCoaster, LaunchedRollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower) to accept and forward a char to super. Ensure RollerCoaster's constructor parameter type matches Ride's.
2) Or, if String was intended, update the UML/problem statement to declare abbreviation as String and modify RollerCoaster's constructor to accept String (public RollerCoaster(String name, String abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings)) and pass a String to super. Ensure all artifacts use the same type so code compiles and students have a single authoritative specification.
